headline: Bank of America CEO has sobering verdict on the economy
triage_reason: Bank of America CEO gave a sobering view on the economy, no new data disclosed.
snippet: Economic resilience is probably something most Americans would welcome. We’re seeing that consumer spending is still growing, wage gains haven’t gone away, and corporate dealmaking is showing fresh momentum. Those trends point to a country that is successfully blowing past the recent inflation shock. However, in an exclusive interview with CBS News' "Face the Nation," Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan sees something more troubling beneath the surface. The economy is arguably holding its own, but the relief households expected hasn’t followed. Food, housing, and fuel costs remain painful, while the strongest spending growth continues to come from consumers with the greatest financial cushions. For investors and households, the next phase could look very different from the soft landing many had anticipated. Economic growth isn’t disappearing, but interestingly, that relentless pace of expansion might compel an economic response few people are prepared for. Moynihan warns inflation could outlast the recovery Moynihan’s big concern is that inflation will likely remain sticky enough to prevent the relief everyone is expecting. “It’s drifting down, and it’s drifting down slower than people would like it,” he said, pointing to continued pressure from housing, food, fuel, and other essential costs. The problem extends beyond prices at the pump. Earlier, they were required to visit the toll plaza physically and submit supporting documents to establish their eligibility, it added. The initiative leverages consent-based integration with government digital platforms, including DigiLocker and VAHAN, to automatically retrieve verified details relating to the commuter’s address, vehicle number and linked FASTag. Local pass eligibility is further established through GIS-based verification, according to the NHAI. The help centre provides assistance on FASTag recharge, KYC requirements, refund status, annual and local pass services and other frequently asked queries. National highway users can also lodge complaints through the help centre, which are automatically routed to the department concerned for grievance resolution. ‘MargMitra’ also allows users to check FASTag blacklisting status, view pending e-notices and report road safety concerns such as stalled vehicles or encroachments on national highways, the NHAI said.

headline: 포티투마루, ‘글로벌 디지털 포럼’서 K-팔란티어 육성을 위한 ‘국방 AI 생태계’ 전략 제시

snippet: 에이전틱 인공지능(AI) 스타트업 포티투마루가 21일 대한상공회의소에서 열린 '2026 제2차 글로벌 디지털 포럼'에 참가해 국방 AI 전환(AX) 전략과 비전을 발표했다. 정보세계정치학회와 서울대학교 미래전연구센터가 공동 주최한 이번 행사는 'AI 기업의 국방 진출과 한국 AI 방산'을 주제로 민·관·학 전문가들이 모여 K-팔란티어의 실현 가능성을 집중 논의했다. 포티투마루 로고 발표자로 나선 정휘웅 포티투마루 CBO 겸 언어지능연구소장은 정부의 핵심 정책인 '한국형 팔란티어·안두릴 육성'과 관련해 발상의 전환을 촉구했다. 특정 기술이나 단일 대기업 중심의 독점 구조로 접근할 경우 오히려 혁신 속도가 늦어질 수 있다는 분석이다. 정 소장은 미국 팔란티어의 본질을 빅데이터 분석으로 고객의 운영 문제를 해결하는 '전방배치 엔지니어(FDE)' 모델로 규정하며, 현장의 문제를 소프트웨어로 즉각 해결하는 방식이 핵심이라고 짚었다. 특히 대형언어모델(LLM)의 확산이 후발주자인 한국에게는 전략적 기회가 될 것으로 내다봤다. 대규모 개발 조직 없이도 현장 실무자가 LLM의 지원을 받아 스스로 필요한 솔루션을 개발할 수 있는 환경이 조성됐기 때문이다. 이는 수십 년간 굳어진 조직 문화나 인력 구조의 한계를 극복할 수 있는 강력한 도구가 될 전망이다. 포티투마루는 성공적인 한국형 방산 AI 생태계 구축을 위해 구체적인 3단계 실행 전략을 제안했다. 주요 내용은 다음과 같다. ▲방산 실무자에게 LLM 기반 개발 권한을 부여하는 '방산 FDE 육성' ▲개별 FDE가 개발한 솔루션을 방위산업계 전체가 공유하고 활용하는 '국방 GitHub' 구축 ▲FDE 출신 인재들의 방산 AI 스타트업 창업 지원 및 제도 개선이다. 정 소장은 특정 플랫폼에 대한 종속 리스크도 강하게 경고했다. 최근 스위스 국방부가 데이터 유출 우려로 팔란티어와의 계약을 취소한 사례를 언급하며, 한국 역시 데이터와 LLM 등 소프트웨어 진입점을 선점해야 한다고 역설했다. 이를 K-방산의 제조 역량과 결합하는 '분산·개방형 선순환 생태계'를 이식해야 한다는 제언이다. 포티투마루는 검색증강생성(RAG42)과 인공지능 독해(MRC42) 등 독보적인 원천기술을 바탕으로 초거대 AI의 고질적 문제인 환각 현상을 제어하고 있다. 보안이 중시되는 국방 환경에 최적화된 프라이빗 모드와 엔터프라이즈 최적화 기술을 통해 비용 효율적인 산업 및 공공 AX 혁신을 지원하는 상태다. 김동환 포티투마루 대표는 "진정한 K-팔란티어의 완성은 소수 기업의 시장 독점이 아니라 현장의 지식이 국방 AI 플랫폼으로 전환되는 건강한 생태계에 달려 있다"고 강조했다. 이어 "국방의 언어를 이해하는 특화 파운데이션 모델을 통해 개발 성과가 방위산업 전체의 자산이 되는 구조를 만드는 데 힘을 보태겠다"고 밝혔다. 비지니스코리아 허성수 기자 (pr@businesskorea.co.kr)

snippet: 롯데카드가 지난 16일 서울 종로구 본사에서 글로벌 아동권리 전문 NGO 굿네이버스와 '기후위기 대응 및 시민 참여형 사회공헌을 위한 업무협약'을 체결했다고 밝혔다. 이번 협약식에는 전계완 롯데카드 전략기획실장과 어정욱 굿네이버스 ESG사회공헌협력실장 등 주요 관계자들이 참석해 중장기적 협력 체계 구축을 약속했다. ▲ (왼쪽부터) 전계완 롯데카드 전략기획실장, 어정욱 굿네이버스 ESG사회공헌협력실장. 양 기관은 이번 협약을 바탕으로 환경 보호와 나눔 문화를 결합한 다양한 프로그램을 공동 기획한다. 특히 각자가 보유한 전문성과 네트워크를 활용해 기후위기에 대한 사회적 공감대를 넓히고 시민들이 자발적으로 참여할 수 있는 장을 마련하는 데 집중할 방침이다. 협약의 핵심 사업인 '2026 굿네이버스 레이스'는 러닝과 환경보호, 나눔을 하나로 묶은 시민 참여형 캠페인이다. 참가자들이 일정 거리를 달리면 그 활동이 기부로 연결되거나 환경 개선 활동에 반영되는 구조로 설계됐다. 행사는 오는 9월 12일 서울에서 첫발을 뗀다. 이후 광주와 부산으로 지역을 넓혀 순차적으로 개최될 예정이다. 롯데카드는 전국 주요 도시를 잇는 이번 레이스를 통해 기후위기 대응의 중요성을 전국적으로 확산시키고 지속가능한 나눔 문화를 정착시킬 것으로 기대하고 있다. 이번 협력은 롯데카드의 ESG 브랜드인 '띵크어스(THINK US & EARTH)' 전략의 연장선에 있다. 롯데카드는 그동안 환경과 사회를 위한 다양한 활동을 전개해 왔으며, 이번 굿네이버스와의 파트너십을 통해 그 범위를 시민 참여형 프로그램으로 대폭 확장하게 됐다. 롯데카드 관계자는 "이번 협약은 일상 속에서 환경 보호와 나눔을 함께 실천할 수 있는 사회공헌 모델을 확대하는 의미 있는 출발점"이라며 "앞으로도 다양한 프로젝트를 통해 지속가능한 ESG 활동을 이어 나가겠다"라고 말했다. 어정욱 굿네이버스 ESG사회공헌협력실장은 "롯데카드와의 협력을 통해 더 많은 시민이 기후위기 대응과 나눔 활동에 참여할 수 있는 기회를 확대하고, 지속가능한 사회공헌 문화를 함께 만들어가겠다"라고 말했다. 비지니스코리아 허성수 기자 (pr@businesskorea.co.kr)

headline: SVC invests in SEEDRA Ventures Fund II to back Saudi tech startups
triage_reason: SVC invests in a fund backing Saudi tech startups; no specific company or amount that could move earnings.
snippet: Saudi Venture Capital (SVC) has invested in SEEDRA Ventures Fund II, a venture capital fund managed by SEEDRA Ventures, to support early-stage, high-growth technology startups in Saudi Arabia. Launched by SEEDRA Ventures, which was founded in 2019, the fund targets startups across sectors including artificial intelligence (AI), fintech, proptech, SaaS, logistics, and other technology-enabled industries, with a focus on companies at the early stages of growth. Through the investment, SVC aims to expand access to institutional capital for Saudi founders, in line with its strategy of supporting startups from the pre-seed stage through pre-IPO. Press release: Saudi Venture Capital (SVC) has announced its investment in SEEDRA Ventures Fund II, a venture capital fund managed by SEEDRA Ventures, an entity licensed by the Capital Market Authority of Saudi Arabia. While sector-agnostic, the Fund is geared towards technology and tech-enabled startups, including Artificial Intelligence (AI), FinTech, and Proptech. The Fund primarily targets early-stage, high-growth startups. Nora Alsarhan, CEO at SVC, said: "Early-stage venture capital investment is where Saudi Arabia's founders meet their first institutional partners, and the depth of that segment shapes what follows. Our investment in SEEDRA Ventures Fund II supports a manager focused squarely on backing Saudi technology founders at that critical stage, expanding the specialised capital available to them and reinforcing the private-sector engine of Vision 2030." "Saudi Arabia is producing some of the most ambitious founders and compelling venture opportunities in the region. SVC's investment, alongside the strong demand that resulted in Fund II being oversubscribed, reinforces our conviction in the market and our ability to identify exceptional entrepreneurs early in their journey. Through Fund II, we will partner with founders as they scale their businesses by providing capital, expertise, and strategic access to our network, while maintaining a disciplined approach to delivering attractive long-term returns for our investors," said Haitham Alforaih, Managing Partner of SEEDRA Ventures. SVC is an investment company established in 2018. It is a subsidiary of the SME Bank, part of the National Development Fund. SVC aims to stimulate and sustain financing for startups and SMEs from pre-Seed to pre-IPO through investment in funds and direct investment in startups and SMEs.

headline: Anara Impact Capital leads $1.45 million investment in Egypt's Reme-D
triage_reason: Anara Impact Capital leads a $1.45 million investment in Egypt's Reme‑D, a small early‑stage amount.
snippet: Egyptian healthtech startup Reme-D has raised $1.45 million in a Pre-Series A funding round led by Anara Impact Capital, with participation from the Global Innovation Fund, Africa Health Ventures, and other investors, to expand its manufacturing capacity, regional footprint, and diagnostic product portfolio. Founded in 2023 by Salma Tammam, Reme-D develops and manufactures molecular diagnostic tests for diseases including tuberculosis (TB), HIV, hepatitis, and HPV, with a focus on delivering affordable, temperature-resilient diagnostics for underserved markets across Africa. The new funding will also support the development of new diagnostics for genetic diseases and cancer, alongside expanding production capacity by tenfold. Last April, Reme-D secured a $500,000 investment from the Global Innovation Fund (GIF) to scale its molecular diagnostics solutions. Press release: Reme-D, an Egyptian healthtech company developing and manufacturing molecular diagnostic solutions, has closed a $1.45 million Pre-Series A funding round led by Anara Impact Capital, with participation from the Global Innovation Fund, Africa Health Ventures, and other investors. Founded with the aim of making advanced diagnostics more accessible across Africa and other underserved markets, Reme-D develops accurate, fast, affordable, and temperature-resilient diagnostic tests for diseases including TB, HIV, hepatitis, and HPV (a leading cause of cervical cancer in women). The funds from this round will help Reme-D expand its manufacturing capacity, regional reach, and product portfolio. The company plans to add tests for new disease areas, including genetic diseases and cancer-related tests, while making more of them temperature-resilient and easier to transport and store in remote locations and in healthcare facilities with limited infrastructure. Since 2023, Reme-D has developed and commercialised 30 diagnostic products at its manufacturing facility in Cairo and supplied over 550,000 tests across Egypt, Kenya, and Sudan. The company supplies both public and private laboratories, hospitals, and research institutions, and its products have been used in international scientific publications. Reme-D has also filed a US patent application covering its proprietary technology. Most recently, Reme-D successfully equipped a custom-made solar-powered mobile laboratory commissioned by the WHO Egypt country office to contribute to the Egyptian Ministry of Health's monitoring of vector-borne diseases

headline: FLOATY Studio secures $1 million from Merak Capital
triage_reason: FLOATY Studio secures $1 million from Merak Capital, a modest seed‑stage financing.
snippet: Saudi Arabia-based FLOATY Studio has raised $1 million in a funding round led by Merak Capital through the Merak Gaming Fund. Founded in 2023 by Fahad Qaysi, Zeyad Almalki and Abdullah Salah, FLOATY Studio develops casual mobile games for international audiences and is currently building two titles: Pirasea, a pirate-themed strategy game, and Hero Squad, a sci-fi action game. The fresh capital will be used to accelerate the development of the company's gaming portfolio, strengthen its production capabilities, and support its international growth strategy as it seeks to establish Saudi-developed intellectual property in global markets. Press release: Saudi mobile game developer FLOATY Studio has raised $1 million in a funding round led by Merak Capital through the Merak Gaming Fund (MGF), as the company looks to accelerate game development and expand its reach in global mobile gaming markets. Founded in 2023, FLOATY Studio develops casual and hybrid-casual mobile games designed for international audiences, focusing on accessible gameplay combined with long-term player engagement. The studio is currently developing two flagship titles: Pirasea, a pirate-themed strategy game, and Hero Squad, a sci-fi action game centred on assembling heroes to battle robotic enemies. The fresh capital will be used to accelerate the development of the company's gaming portfolio, strengthen its production capabilities, and support its international growth strategy as it seeks to establish Saudi-developed intellectual property in global markets. The investment was made through the Merak Gaming Fund, an $80 million vehicle established to support high-potential gaming startups and strengthen Saudi Arabia's game development ecosystem. The fund has previously invested in gaming companies, including Qwacks and Khosouf Studio, as part of its broader strategy to foster local talent and globally competitive game studios. Merak Capital said the investment reflects its confidence in FLOATY Studio's product vision and in Saudi Arabia's growing position as a regional hub for gaming entrepreneurship. The funding also aligns with the Kingdom's broader efforts to develop a globally competitive gaming industry by supporting homegrown studios capable of creating original content for international audiences.

headline: Iran's Araghchi congratulates Khalil al-Hayya as new head of Hamas' political bureau
triage_reason: Iran's Araghchi congratulates new head of Hamas' political bureau; political but not a war escalation.
snippet: Iran's Araghchi congratulates Khalil al-Hayya as new head of Hamas' political bureau The Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi in a message to the newly appointed head of Hamas' political bureau, Khalil al-Hayyah, congratulated him on his position. "I sincerely congratulate you on your election as the new head of the Political Bureau of the Islamic Resistance Movement - Hamas," Araghchi told Hayya according to state news agency IRNA. The Iranian foreign minister also "honoured the memory" of previous leaders within the Palestinian movement, emphasising Iran's continued support for the "legitimate struggles of the Palestinian people to be freed from the occupation, apartheid, and colonialism of the genocidal Zionist regime".

headline: After deadly weekend for US troops, Trump vows revenge
triage_reason: After a deadly weekend for US troops, Trump vows revenge; political rhetoric without concrete policy change.
snippet: President Donald Trump on Monday said Iran would "pay" for killing US soldiers after multiple service members were killed over the weekend as part of the United States' war against Iran, marking one of the deadliest days for US forces since the war started in February. The number of U.S. troops killed in the war on Iran rose to 17 over the weekend, with the remains of an additional service member being examined. Two of the personnel were confirmed to have been killed when Iran attacked U.S. personnel in Jordan . "Every time Iran kills an American Soldier they will pay for that killing many times over," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "This directive has been passed on to Secretary of War, Pete Hegseth, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, Daniel Caine." In March, six U.S. troops were killed when an Iranian drone slammed into a U.S. military facility in Port ​Shuaiba, Kuwait. Roughly 430 U.S. troops have been injured in the conflict so far. The White House said Trump would attend the dignified transfer at Dover Air Force Base in Delaware for the service members killed. It is unclear what specific "directive" Trump passed to the Pentagon. But a U.S. official told news agency Reuters that prior to the deadly attack in Jordan, the United States had already started moving additional military aircraft, including fighter jets and refueling tankers, to the Middle East. Joe Kent, who headed the National Counterterrorism Center until March, said the back and forth between U.S. and Iranian forces risked further escalation. "Get our troops out now before we suffer a mass casualty attack. Break the escalation trap," Kent, who resigned over Trump's war in Iran, wrote on X. In the past week, Trump has threatened to expand the targets being struck in Iran to include energy plants and bridges, sending ground forces to seize Iran’s Kharg Island oil hub and bombing a deep-underground nuclear-linked site known as Pickaxe ​Mountain. News agency Reuters , citing sources, reported that recent waves of U.S. strikes on Iran aimed at ​forcing open the Strait of Hormuz are also targeting Iranian military capabilities the U.S. would want to destroy before executing more complex operations against ‌Iran. The war, including its monetary cost, is set to dominate a congressional hearing on Tuesday with Hegseth and Caine.
